chapter: Clarinet teachers and the Baton Rouge scene
title: Ragtime for dancing and the church objection
summary: The bands played only for dancing, mostly ensemble with every third number a waltz, called it ragtime, and some church people thought it evil.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: They say Chris Kelly did the same thing, get out and talk with the people and all that stuff, and leave the band play. But let me ask you what kind of things they played. Because you said the Catholic Church used to put on dances. Were they strictly for dancing? Or they didn't play concerts or anything? What did they play?
All of it was strictly for dancing, as I remember. There wasn't anything as a concert. Most of it was ensemble. Every third number was a waltz.
What would they have called the music that they played at that time?
Yes. They called it a ragtime band.
Would you have called it that?
That's what we called it. And a lot of them old church people didn't like that. A lot of them wouldn't go, and said that was evil music.
